Full-file runs used --ratio 6:2 on 8 CPUs; all repro cases and Tcl reruns for this triage used --ratio 3:1 on CPUs 36-39 (fresh servers; 2s AND 1s were rerun in isolation for every independent root). build/h5reach/final/report.json.gz was checked row by row against final-a/final-b: identical failing sets. 'hung' and 'where' come from the full-file and reach evidence: 'unit/multi: Blocking commands ignores the timeout' is hung=false (it errored in the full-file run behind the MULTI cascade) but HANGS on a fresh server (MULTI-XREADGROUP-BLOCK-HANG). run_file's SO_REUSEADDR probe bind can fail with EADDRINUSE for ~60 s on a port that only holds TIME-WAIT sockets from a killed server; use another port or wait. CASCADES: (1) unit/tracking -- TRACK-BCAST-BATCH is the only first-half root: 'The connection gets invalidation messages about all the keys' (then the prefix test) leaves extra one-key invalidations in $rd_redirection, so every later read is shifted; 'RESP3 Client gets tracking-redir-broken...' then reads a stale message instead of the QUIT 'OK' and aborts before recreating $rd_redirection, r keeps REDIRECT to the dead client and accumulates tracking-redir-broken pushes; once the stale queue drains the next read hits EOF ('I/O error reading reply'), redis.tcl silently reconnects the deferred client and the following read waits forever on a fresh unsubscribed socket = the hang. The hang point moves because the active-expire invalidation for mykey{t} lands before or after that read (one-message offset); that offset is also the only reason 'Different clients using different protocols can track the same key' passed in reach-2s and failed in reach-1s -- not a mode difference. All 11 tests from the redir-broken test to 'hdel deliver...' pass on 2s and 1s with an in-sync redirection client. The 5th tracking hang ('...tracking table key eviction') is independent (fresh: TRACK-MAXKEYS-IMMUTABLE). (2) unit/pause -- every failing pause test returns before 'client unpause', leaving a 60-100 s PAUSE WRITE armed that holds the next test's first write past the idle deadline; that explains four of the six discovery hangs; the two RO-script tests hang on a FRESH server (PAUSE-SCRIPT-FLAGS); only 'Test read/admin multi-execs are not blocked by pause RO' is a pure cascade. (3) unit/multi -- 'DISCARD should not fail during OOM' aborts before DISCARD and before 'config set maxmemory 0', so the main client stays inside MULTI with maxmemory 1 for the rest of the file: 5 tests are pure cascades ('MULTI calls can not be nested', 'Command not allowed inside a transaction'), the others fail on their own roots in a fresh run. (4) unit/protocol -- 'test large number of args' and 'test argument rewriting - issue 9598' are cascades of 'RESP3 attributes readraw' (aborts on DEBUG PROTOCOL with readraw/deferred left on); a rerun skipping it passes both in 2s and 1s. (5) unit/pubsub -- 'publish to self inside multi' gets 3 receivers because two earlier failing keyspace tests never close their 'psubscribe *' clients: the listpackex test (UNSUP-ENCODING, cited) and the stream-events test (PUBSUB-IMPLICIT-CONSUMER-EVENT); the cascade survives a fix of either one alone. MODE DIFFERENCES: none that are real. In the original 6:2 full-file run the 2s multi script-timeout tests saw '$r2 EXEC' answer 'EXECABORT ... execution error' where 1s answered '-OOM ...'; a traced 3:1 rerun gave -OOM in both -- a geometry-dependent view of MULTI-OOM-EXEC through the leftover maxmemory 1. SLOWLOG-MAXLEN-PER-THREAD counts depend on the thread layout (max-len 3 -> 2s 4 entries, 1s 5; a 6:2 isolated 'max entries' rerun passed). JUDGMENT CALLS: MIGRATE is treated as part of the deliberately absent cluster family (COMMAND LIST diff vs Redis 7.4.10: TomoKV lacks exactly cluster*, migrate, module*, psync, replconf, sync) -> 'MIGRATE command is marked with movablekeys', 'MONITOR supports redacting command arguments', 'SLOWLOG - Some commands can redact sensitive fields' are class 1; if MIGRATE should exist they are REAL. maxmemory-clients (client eviction) and the hidden test-only knobs rdb-key-save-delay/key-load-delay are class 2 (memory / persistence-timing internals); 'CONFIG SET rollback on set error' otherwise rolls back correctly. 'CONFIG sanity' first trips on hll-sparse-max-bytes (class 2 alone) but also on port/bind/tls-auth-clients (REAL) and TomoKV-only boot knobs (thread-mode, net-io, ...), hence REAL. Merged roots: MULTI-POLICY-REFUSAL = FLUSHALL-in-MULTI (unit/lazyfree) + UNSUBSCRIBE-in-MULTI (unit/pubsub), both multi_engine_policy_refusal ('Owner decision group 5'); LAZYFREE-COUNTERS also covers the tracking eviction test (same missing lazyfree_pending_objects). REPRO CAVEATS: CLIENT-LIST-CMD-NAME and RESET-CLEARS-LIBNAME compare a CLIENT INFO line that also carries volatile per-connection fields, so read cmd=client vs cmd=client|info and lib-name= vs lib-name=redis.py in repros.json (upstream: ./runtest --single unit/introspection --only "CLIENT LIST with IDs"; --only "CLIENT SETINFO can set a library name to this connection" --only "RESET does NOT clean library name"). PAUSE-BLOCKED-COUNT compares the whole INFO clients reply (TomoKV prints 4 of Redis's 13 fields); the discriminating field is blocked_clients (Redis 1, TomoKV 0) (upstream: ./runtest --single unit/pause --only "Test write commands are paused by RO"). INFO-MISSING-FIELDS: Redis's CPU numbers are volatile, the defect is TomoKV's empty bulk. OBJECT-IDLETIME-ZERO: Redis answers 2 or 3 depending on clock alignment, TomoKV 0. CONNECTED-CLIENTS-LAG reproduced 6/6 per mode; the stale count clears within ~1 s even when idle. SECONDARY FINDINGS (not the first failure of any B1 test): EVAL bodies with a '#!lua' shebang (with or without flags=) fail to compile on TomoKV -- only FUNCTION LOAD parses shebangs; it sits behind PAUSE-SCRIPT-FLAGS/PAUSE-BLOCKED-COUNT in the pause script tests (case EVAL-SHEBANG-UNPARSED, DIFFERENT in 2s and 1s). CLIENT TRACKING REDIRECT is briefly accepted for a client that has just QUIT (Redis: 'does not exist'), probably the same deferred-release window as CONNECTED-CLIENTS-LAG; it feeds the tracking chain (probe parts/T-probe-quit.py).
